name: CharacterEval
ontology_notes: Chinese role-playing conversational-agent eval, not a memory engine and not a memory bench. Tu et al. arXiv 2401.01275v2. 77 leading characters from Chinese novels and scripts. 1,785 multi-turn dialogues. Table 1. Average 9.28 turns and 369.69 tokens per conversation. 6,811 train plus 4,564 test examples (11,375, paper abstract says 11,376). Profiles crawled from Baidu Baike. Thirteen metrics on four dimensions. Conversational fluency, coherence, consistency. Knowledge exposure, accuracy, hallucination. Persona behavior and utterance. Attractiveness human-likeness, communication skill, expression diversity, empathy. MBTI personality back-test. CharacterRM (Baichuan2-13B) scores the subjective twelve. User modeled is a novel or script character in a short scene. Metric scores next-response RP quality against a profile. Misses holes 1 as 50+ sessions (session-scale identity only), 2 social timing, 3 joke-as-fact, 4 retcon, 5 cross-character leak, 6 lore versus lived event, 7 poisoning, 8 cost per turn, 9 forget-that, 10 three-month reunion.

supersession.evidence: No knowledge-update task. The model sees a static profile plus the current dialogue context and writes the next line. §3 Problem Formulation.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Average 9.28 turns per conversation. No dated facts, session timestamps, or reunion probes. Table 1.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: A character profile P is distinct from dialogue context C_n. That is persona versus transcript, not user versus character versus relationship versus lore in a store.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Metrics reward knowledge exposure and attractiveness. No do-not-recall or socially-wrong-time items.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Knowledge hallucination (KH) is character-canon error, not a stored jailbreak of a system persona.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that. Profile is always available.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Reported numbers are CharacterRM or GPT-4 Likert-style scores and MBTI accuracy. No tokens-per-turn or LLM-calls-per-turn meter.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: MIT LICENSE. Data and scripts run locally. CharacterRM is Hugging Face morecry/BaichuanCharRM. Closed models in the paper use vendor APIs.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Session-scale Chinese RP identity metrics. Would prefer models that stay in character for about nine turns. Would not select a long-term companion memory system. Not a memory bench.

published_eval.name: CharacterEval
published_eval.claimed_score: Table 2. CharacterRM overall Pearson with humans 0.631 versus GPT-4 1-shot 0.362. Table 4 CharacterRM. BC-NPC-Turbo leads character-consistency average 2.764 and attractiveness average 2.946. MiniMax 2.718 / 2.902. GPT-4 personality back-test 0.694, MiniMax 0.685. GPT-4 is weaker on Chinese RP conversation metrics than the Chinese RP-specialized APIs.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Next-utterance roleplay quality for a Chinese novel or script character given a Baike profile and a short multi-turn context. Twelve subjective metrics via CharacterRM plus MBTI accuracy. Not long-term memory.

open_unknowns: README claims 23,020 examples. Paper abstract says 11,376. Table 1 sums to 11,375 (6,811+4,564). Card follows the paper table.
